Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration had no causal effect on depressive symptoms.
Sentence: "MR analysis revealed no causal effects of 25(OH)vitamin D concentration, either on DS (inverse variance weighted (IVW); b = 0.025, SE = 0.038, p = 0.52) or on BD (IVW; b = 0.020, SE = 0.012, p = 0.10)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (DS)
Population: Genetic summary data: 161,460 participants for depressive symptoms GWAS; SUNLIGHT GWAS of 79,366 subjects for 25(OH)D instruments
Intervention: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration (six SNPs)
Comparator: None (Mendelian randomization)
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 322,280
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Perceived depression scores improved significantly more in the TRI 360TM multi-ingredient supplement group than in the placebo group.
Sentence: "All assessed perception scorings on psychological symptoms like fatigue, mental stress, sleep disturbance, anxiety, depression, emotional trauma, mood changes, self-confidence, willpower, and motivation were very significantly (p ≤ 0.0001) improved in TRI 360TM participants than placebo control group."
Measured as: depression perception scoring
Population: Adults aged 20-45 years with one or more psychological symptoms
Intervention: TRI 360TM proprietary nutraceutical combination capsules twice a day, up to 180 days
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 84
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
